items.feedText: Die übrigen 11 Prozent sind unentschlossen. Das zeigt eine repräsentative Forsa-Umfrage für das Deutsche Schulportal. items.articleBody:
# Repräsentative Umfrage: Das sagen Lehrer zur Arbeitszeiterfassung

Seit den Urteilen des Europäischen Gerichtshofs und des Bundesarbeitsgerichts ist gerichtlich bestätigt, dass eine Arbeitszeiterfassung zum Gesundheitsschutz vorgeschrieben ist. Wird sie bald auch für Lehrkräfte eingeführt? © Getty Was für die meisten Arbeitnehmerinnen und Arbeitnehmer in Deutschland eine Selbstverständlichkeit ist, gilt für Lehrkräfte als umstritten. Seit einem Urteil des Europäischen Gerichtshofs aus dem Jahr 2019 und einer Entscheidung des Bundesarbeitsgerichts aus dem Jahr 2022 ist auch gerichtlich bestätigt, dass die Erfassung der gesamten tatsächlichen Arbeitszeit zum Gesundheitsschutz zwingend vorgeschrieben ist. Die KMK pochte auf eine Sonderregelung für Schulen, das Bundesarbeitsministerium bekräftigte, dass es keine Ausnahmen für den Schulbereich geben würde. Wie stehen aber die Lehrkräfte selbst zu einer verpflichtenden Erfassung ihrer Arbeitszeit?

Neue Daten, die dem Deutschen Schulportal exklusiv vorliegen, zeigen nun erstmals, dass eine Mehrheit der Lehrkräfte in Deutschland die Einführung einer verpflichtenden Arbeitszeiterfassung befürwortet. 55 Prozent sind dafür, 34 Prozent dagegen. Weitere 11 Prozent sind bei dem Thema noch unentschlossen. Zu diesem Ergebnis kommt eine Umfrage, die das Meinungsforschungsinstitut Forsa im Auftrag der Robert Bosch Stiftung für das Deutsche Schulportal durchgeführt hat. Im September 2026 wurden insgesamt 1.056 Lehrkräfte an allgemeinbildenden und berufsbildenden Schulen in ganz Deutschland befragt. Die statistische Fehlermarge für die gesamte Lehrerschaft beträgt bis zu drei Prozentpunkte.

© Henriette Anders Infografik herunterladen Eine Zustimmung zur Arbeitszeiterfassung gibt es in fast allen befragten Gruppen. Besonders hoch ist sie bei Lehrkräften an Gymnasien, von denen 60 Prozent eine verpflichtende Erfassung befürworten. An Haupt-, Real- und Gesamtschulen liegt der Wert bei 56 Prozent, an Grundschulen bei 51 Prozent und an beruflichen Schulen bei 49 Prozent. Auch unter Schulleitungen und stellvertretenden Schulleitungen befürwortet eine Mehrheit die Arbeitszeiterfassung: 56 Prozent sind dafür, 35 Prozent lehnen sie ab.

## Warum viele Lehrkräfte eine Erfassung ihrer Arbeitszeiten wünschen

Doch was erhoffen sich Lehrkräfte von der Arbeitszeiterfassung? Die mit Abstand häufigste Antwort auf die offen gestellte Frage lautet: mehr Transparenz über die tatsächliche Arbeitsbelastung. Unter den Befürworterinnen und Befürwortern nennen 70 Prozent die Sichtbarmachung ihrer Arbeitszeiten und ihrer Arbeitsbelastung als wichtigstes Argument für die Einführung einer verpflichtenden Erfassung.

23 Prozent der Befürworterinnen und der Befürworter hoffen auf mehr Gerechtigkeit und Vergleichbarkeit zwischen Lehrkräften und Fächern. Weitere 15 Prozent nennen den Gesundheitsschutz und die Prävention von Überlastung, während 14 Prozent eine angemessene Vergütung oder Entschädigung für Überstunden als wichtigsten Grund anführen. 9 Prozent hoffen, dass die Erfassung der Arbeitszeiten dazu beiträgt, gesellschaftlichen Vorurteilen gegenüber dem Lehrerberuf entgegenzuwirken. Die Gründe für die Befürwortung oder die Ablehnung einer verpflichtenden Arbeitszeiterfassung wurden ohne vorgegebene Antwortoptionen anhand offener Fragen erhoben, wobei Mehrfachnennungen zulässig waren.

> Seit ich meine Arbeitsbelastung in der App erfasse, plane ich meine Woche deutlich bewusster.

Der Bremer Lehrer Björn Wolf erlebt bereits, wie die Arbeitszeiterfassung den Schulalltag verändern kann. Bremen ist in diesem Schuljahr als erstes Bundesland mit einem Pilotprojekt zur Arbeitszeiterfassung an Schulen gestartet. Wolf unterrichtet an der Oberschule an der Lerchenstraße, einer der teilnehmenden Schulen.

Auf der Fachtagung „Lehrkräftearbeitszeit als Hebel für gute Schule” am 4. November 2026 in Bremen schilderte er seine Erfahrungen: „Seit ich meine Arbeitsbelastung in der App erfasse, plane ich meine Woche deutlich bewusster“, berichtet Wolf. „Ich sehe, wie viele Stunden mir zur Verfügung stehen, und kann dann gezielt entscheiden: An welchen Tagen habe ich Unterricht? Wann bleibt Zeit zum Vorbereiten? Und wann passen die übrigen Aufgaben hinein?“ Die Tagung wurde vom Senator für Kinder und Bildung der Freien Hansestadt Bremen, der Telekom Stiftung, die das Bremer Pilotprojekt fachlich begleitet , der Deutschen Gesellschaft für Bildungsverwaltung und dem Netzwerk Schulentwicklung veranstaltet.

Auch der Leiter der Oberschule an der Lerchenstraße, Jonathan Dauber, sieht Chancen für einen besseren Arbeitsschutz. Vor allem jüngere Lehrkräfte an seiner Schule seien oft ständig erreichbar und täten sich schwer, Grenzen zwischen Arbeit und Privatleben zu ziehen. „Die Arbeitszeiterfassung kann helfen, ohne schlechtes Gewissen zu sagen: Jetzt bin ich nicht erreichbar.“

## Jede dritte Lehrkraft lehnt eine verpflichtende Arbeitszeiterfassung ab

Dennoch stößt die verpflichtende Arbeitszeiterfassung auch auf erheblichen Widerstand. Laut der Umfrage lehnen 34 Prozent der Lehrkräfte sie ab. Ihr häufigstes Argument ist, dass sich die tatsächlichen Arbeitszeiten im Lehrerberuf nur schwer zuverlässig erfassen lassen.

Unter den Gegnerinnen und Gegnern geben 40 Prozent als wichtigsten Grund an, dass die Arbeitszeiten von Lehrkräften praktisch nicht erfassbar, messbar oder kontrollierbar seien. Weitere 23 Prozent befürchten bürokratischen Mehraufwand, während 21 Prozent Bedenken haben, an Flexibilität einzubüßen oder eine Atmosphäre wachsenden Misstrauens zu schaffen. Seltener genannt werden die Vermischung von Privat- und Berufsleben (11 Prozent), Zweifel am grundsätzlichen Nutzen (8 Prozent) und die Gefahr eines Missbrauchs (7 Prozent).

Bedenken gegenüber der Arbeitszeiterfassung wurden auch auf der Fachtagung in Bremen deutlich. Sven Räther, stellvertretender Schulleiter des Hamburger Gymnasiums Ohmoor, stellte infrage, ob eine minutengenaue Erfassung mit den Realitäten des Lehrberufs vereinbar ist. „In der Theorie klingt das gut“, so Räther. „Aber eine Lehrkraft kann nicht sagen: ‚Die Arbeitszeit ist jetzt vorbei, lieber Schüler, ich habe keine Zeit mehr für dich.‘ Das ist entscheidend, denn genau dieser Teil macht unseren Beruf so besonders.“

Auch Jan Riedel, Bildungsminister des Landes Sachsen-Anhalt, äußert sich auf der Konferenz skeptisch. Er argumentierte, der Debatte fehle ein klar definiertes Ziel. Gehe es darum, die Schulen zu verbessern, eine gerechtere Verteilung der Arbeitsbelastung zu erreichen oder eine übermäßige Arbeitsbelastung sichtbar zu machen? „Ich befürchte, dass wir Erwartungen wecken, aber nicht klar definieren, was unser eigentliches Ziel ist“, sagt er.

## Bremen erprobt als erstes Bundesland die Arbeitszeiterfassung

Seit August 2026 erfassen in Bremen und Bremerhaven rund 700 Beschäftigte an neun Schulen ihre Arbeitszeiten digital mithilfe der App „Untis Arbeitszeit“. Erste Erkenntnisse deuten darauf hin, dass der Zeitaufwand für die einzelnen Einträge relativ gering ist. Laut Projektkoordinator an der Bremer Schulbehörde Kolja Buß sind 50 Prozent der Einträge innerhalb von 32 Sekunden erledigt, während 90 Prozent nicht länger als 82 Sekunden dauern. Ein besonderer Schwerpunkt des Pilotprojektes liegt auf dem Arbeitsschutz. Untersucht wird zudem, wie gesetzliche Ruhezeiten im Schulalltag eingehalten werden können.

Dies kann insbesondere für Lehrkräfte mit kleinen Kindern eine Herausforderung darstellen, die möglicherweise erst spät am Abend Zeit finden, Unterricht vorzubereiten oder Aufgaben zu benoten. „Die Einhaltung der elfstündigen Ruhezeit ist ein Thema, das uns aus den Schulen bisher am häufigsten zurückgemeldet wurde“, berichtet Buß auf der Fachtagung.

## Rackles: Arbeitszeiterfassung könnte zu einer gerechteren Aufgabenverteilung führen

Für den Bremer Bildungssenator Mark Rackles (SPD) stellt die Einführung der Arbeitszeiterfassung einen großen kulturellen Wandel dar. In einem Interview mit dem Deutschen Schulportal im Juli 2026 erklärte er, dass Lehrkräfte bisher nur einen Teil ihrer Arbeitszeit nachweisen mussten. Künftig werde viel transparenter werden, wer wie viele Stunden arbeite.

Er erwartet, dass das System erhebliche Unterschiede in der Arbeitsbelastung zwischen einzelnen Lehrkräften aufzeigen wird. Dies könnte auch unangenehme Konsequenzen haben. Während Lehrkräfte mit besonders hoher Arbeitsbelastung Entlastung benötigen würden, könnte von anderen erwartet werden, zusätzliche Aufgaben zu übernehmen. „Die, die unterhalb des Arbeitssolls sind, müssen mehr arbeiten – das ist völlig klar“, so Rackles im Interview. Das würde jedoch nicht unbedingt mehr Unterrichtsstunden bedeuten. Stattdessen könnten zusätzliche Aufgaben gerechter auf das Kollegium verteilt werden.

## Was geschieht, sobald die Arbeitszeiten erfasst sind?

Doch selbst wenn eine Arbeitszeiterfassung eingeführt wird, bleibt eine entscheidende Frage offen: Was geschieht mit den gesammelten Daten? Rackles sieht die Chance, mit Hilfe der Daten, Aufgaben innerhalb der Schulen gerechter zu verteilen und übermäßige Arbeitsbelastungen abzubauen. Gleichzeitig könnten sie eine Grundlage dafür bieten, zusätzlichen Personalbedarf zu ermitteln und zu begründen.

Auf der Konferenz in Bremen betonte er, dass zusätzliche Mittel in Zeiten knapper öffentlicher Haushalte sorgfältig begründet werden müssen: „Mehr Ressourcen für Bildung geht immer“, sagt Rackles. „In der heutigen Zeit muss man aber sehr präzise sagen, wofür wir mehr Ressourcen brauchen. Wir brauchen konkrete Zahlen statt eines Bauchgefühls. Dieser Debatte muss man sich 2027 stellen.“ Ob eine verpflichtende Arbeitszeiterfassung tatsächlich zur Entlastung der Lehrkräfte führt, wird daher weitgehend davon abhängen, wie Schulen und Bildungsbehörden die erhobenen Daten nutzen.

Die repräsentative Forsa-Umfrage macht erstmals deutlich, dass eine Mehrheit der Lehrkräfte eine verpflichtende Arbeitszeiterfassung grundsätzlich befürwortet.

Mitarbeit: Jasmin Shamsi

# How Google Duplex evolved to also call businesses for you in Gemini

How Google Duplex evolved to also call businesses for you in Gemini November 20, 2026

Yossi Matias, Vice President, Google & GM, Google Research, Yaniv Leviathan, Google Fellow, Google Research, and Janet Zhou, Group Product Manager, Google Maps

When we introduced Google Duplex in 2018, it pioneered natural voice conversations between AI and local businesses over the phone. Since then, this technology has worked behind the scenes across many Google products. These capabilities are integrated directly in Tasks in Gemini .

Completing tasks like making dinner reservations or booking a hair appointment is time consuming. Live phone conversations move fast and rarely follow a script. The person on the other end can say almost anything, often revising their thoughts mid-sentence – and people often rely on subtle tone changes to indicate whose turn it is to speak. Pause half a second too long, and it sounds like the call dropped; speak too soon, and you end up talking over each other. Leveraging AI to complete these tasks respectfully over the phone required us to consider high quality speech understanding, contextual reasoning, and speech synthesis working together in a single, low-latency system.

We introduced Google Duplex nearly a decade ago to help address this challenge. Propelled by advances in foundation models, the Duplex architecture has evolved to power autonomous task completion across many core products, such as Google Search and Maps. This week, we launched Duplex in Tasks in Gemini App , a personal AI collaborator that can help coordinate real-world chores, like calling businesses for you and handling real-world requests on behalf of the user. In this post, we look back at the decade-long architectural evolution that made this possible — moving from early, closed-domain models to a unified stack built entirely with Gemini.

## From closed-domain calls to Tasks in Gemini

What began as a narrow, task-specific system quickly expanded into a shared conversational infrastructure, built in collaboration with teams across Google.

During the COVID-19 pandemic, when business hours and services shifted rapidly, Duplex doubled down on verifying merchant info automatically to keep listings accurate. It remains an important data source; for example, business information sourced from Duplex’s phone calls had been shown in Search and Maps over one trillion times , as we shared in 2023.

Simultaneously, we worked with Android and hardware teams to bring these conversational models directly on-device. Starting in 2019, we rolled out new Pixel Call Assist features across five consecutive Pixel generations. These models continue to power features like Call Screen and Hold for Me , helping users filter unknown callers and speak with a live agent when a hold queue ends until the user rejoins. In 2025 and 2026, foundation models unlocked broader agentic calling in Google Search and Ask Maps , checking quotes, product availability, and service openings from pet grooming to auto repair.

## Three generations of conversational architecture

Over the past decade, the stack behind these calls evolved through three distinct eras, moving from bespoke neural pipelines to a unified architecture using Gemini.

### 1. Pre-LLM closed-domain models

We started work on Google Duplex before modern language models and even before the transformer itself was invented. In these early days, to ensure businesses and users had a great experience, we constrained Duplex to narrow domains and trained custom recurrent neural network models on anonymized, task-specific phone conversations. Without pre-trained world knowledge, we taught our models how to handle every specific type of task efficiently. In practice, this meant relying on extensive training data for each task type — such as interpreting the rigid flow of restaurant booking versus checking holiday hours — to ensure the system could reliably navigate domain-specific logic.

### 2. Early generative models and hybrid stacks

Google Duplex started employing open domain foundation models in production as they emerged. For example, in 2022 Duplex used LaMDA in live calls. These pre-trained models simplified comprehension and common-sense reasoning, allowing the system to handle unexpected conversational turns and tangents, while remaining grounded in the context like a standard restaurant booking.

However, these early generative models were less predictable and sometimes slower than today's, so we built hybrid stacks that paired generative models for flexible phrasing with deterministic state tracking and strict policy guardrails. This helped ensure that both users and businesses had a great experience.

### 3. Unbounded tasks and Gemini integration

As foundation models advanced, we removed the constraint of fixed verticals entirely by shifting to prompting the system with free-text task descriptions. This allowed models to define a task simply via a prompt, enabling the system to generalize to new task types and nuances (like asking for window seating or extra space for a stroller) and new business categories, without building separate dialogue models from scratch.

Our calling stack uses Gemini to unify multimodal understanding, planning, and dialogue generation so the system can navigate multi-constraint requests — like scheduling car maintenance around calendar conflicts — and adapt when a receptionist suggests another slot.

## Technical hurdles in live telephony

Even with frontier models, live telephony poses hurdles that pre-training on standard datasets like the web alone doesn't solve:

- Pragmatic grounding for pre-call and conversational context, and real-world intent understanding: The web doesn’t have all the data needed to capture how calls unfold with busy merchants. Nearly a decade of experience with goal-directed calls helps our stack grasp pragmatic norms, starting even before the call. In practice, this means matching a free-text task with a business based on the historical context of past conversations (e.g., knowing a specific vendor doesn't take reservations for large groups over the weekend) to predict whether a task will work. During the call, this helps the model determine what makes sense to ask at a given moment, how to read polite indirect refusals, and how to keep calls brief and effective.
- Sub-second latency in noisy acoustic setups: Calls run over compressed phone lines against loud backdrops like clattering in kitchens, espresso machines, street noise, and side chatter. Our stack is tuned for low-latency streaming inference so replies land at a natural cadence. Custom acoustic and conversation cadence models assist the core AI system with handling background noise and pauses, stop talking when expected, etc.
## Designing for both ends of the line

Duplex has to work just as well for the business answering the phone as it does for the user. That principle shaped several design choices:

- Clear disclosure. Every call opens by clearly disclosing that it’s an AI agent — specifically, an automated system calling from Google.
- Businesses stay in control. Merchants can opt out of automated calls in their Google Business Profile settings, or simply say “Please stop calling my business” during a call.
- No setup and zero adaptation. Duplex works through the phone a business already answers: no software to install, no booking system to maintain and no staff to train. Whoever answers can handle the call the way they would with any customer, even mid-rush with a line at the counter.
- One conversation, many insights. Details gathered on one call can answer many later questions, so a business isn’t asked the same thing over and over. For example, Google Maps can show details that Duplex gathers about businesses, like happy hour specials, patio seating, pet-friendliness, a parking tip or even a weekly trivia night.
## Conclusion

Many daily errands, local services, and urgent tasks still require speaking directly with another person to coordinate details reliably. By integrating Duplex’s capabilities into Tasks in Gemini App, we are taking another step toward closing this loop. Natural voice interaction becomes a seamlessly integrated modality that the agent can deploy whenever structured digital channels like online APIs or booking forms don't exist. Using our newest Gemini 4 models — including Gemini 4 Hydrogen and Gemini 4 Neon — Tasks in Gemini can now support more comprehensive workflows like analyzing utility bills, processing transactions securely via the Agent Payments Protocol , and coordinating with users over email and Rich Communication Services (RCS). Through these capabilities, we are bringing this research into the next generation of AI assistance.

## Acknowledgements

We’re thankful to the Duplex team and to everyone across Google leading and involved in this decade-long journey.For driving the transition to Gemini-powered calling and making this launch in Tasks in Gemini possible, we're especially grateful to Yoav Tzur, Sasha Goldshtein, Rafael Goldfarb, Liran Peretz, Ritika Pathak, Sen Li, Ran Manor, Dekel Auster, and many others across the team.

items.feedText: Der FC Bayern rettet gegen den 1. FC Köln ein 1:1 ins Ziel – und muss die nächsten beiden Verletzten beklagen: Harry Kane und Michael Olise müssen früh ausgewechselt werden, der Stürmer zieht sich einen Syndesmoseriss zu.
items.articleBody:
# FC Bayern spielt 1:1 gegen Köln: Kane und Olise verletzt - Sport - SZ.de

Harry Kane verletzt sich am linken Fuß und wird dem FC Bayern vorraussichtlich monatelang fehlen. Foto: Tom Weller/dpa Der FC Bayern rettet gegen den 1. FC Köln ein 1:1 ins Ziel – und muss die nächsten beiden Verletzten beklagen: Harry Kane und Michael Olise müssen früh ausgewechselt werden, der Stürmer zieht sich einen Syndesmoseriss zu.

Von Sebastian Fischer

Vincent Kompany , das ist in den vergangenen Wochen zur Genüge geschildert worden, ist ein ausgesprochen akribischer Trainer, der sich auf jedes Spiel ausführlich vorbereitet. Aber ob er schon mal einen Gegner so ausführlich studiert hat wie den 1. FC Köln ? „Ich habe vier Wochen gewartet“, hatte er am Vortag gesagt: „Zeit hatte ich genügend.“ Und seine Motivation sei zwar „sehr hoch für jedes Spiel“. Aber diesmal sei sie noch etwas höher.

FC Bayern München : Vincent Kompany und das komplizierte Comeback von Jamal Musiala Der Bayern-Trainer ist nach seiner Hirnhautreizung mit Arm in der Schlinge zurück auf der Bank – und spricht auch über die anstehende Rückkehr seines Spielmachers. Zu Musialas Vertrag äußert sich nun auch noch Bayern-Boss Jan-Christian Dreesen.

items.subtitle: Die Weltklimakonferenz in der Türkei geht in die Verlängerung.
items.feedText: Gerungen wird laut Medienberichten unter anderem um Formulierungen zu fossilen Brennstoffen. In dem aktuellen Entwurf der Abschlusserklärung wird ein Ausstieg aus Kohle, Öl und Gas nicht direkt erwähnt. Mehrere Länder kündigten ihren Widerstand dagegen an.
items.articleBody:
# Antalya - Weltklimakonferenz geht in die Verlängerung - EU fordert Änderungen

Die Teilnehmer des Klimagipfels Cop31 im türkischen Antalya ringen noch um eine Abschlusserklärung. (Anadolu Agency) Am Abend begann eine Plenumssitzung, bei der allerdings nur technische Fragen erörtert wurden. Die zentralen politischen Entscheidungen blieben ungeklärt. Der türkische Umweltminister und Präsident der Klimakonferenz, Kurum, zeigte sich zuversichtlich, dass eine Einigung möglich ist. Einige Delegierte entrollten ein Protestbanner und warnten vor einem Scheitern der Konferenz. Eine Vertreterin der Europäischen Union sagte in Antalya, der bisherige Entwurf sei nicht ausbalanciert. items.articleBody:
Josh Tafoya's "Bad Hombre" (2026) (image courtesy the artist)

Patricia Belli, Troy Montes Michie, Willy Chavarria, and Camila Falquéz are among the 20 artists and designers who will be featured in *Malvestir*, MoMA PS1's upcoming exhibition on the visual lexicon of Latin American fashion, opening in April 2027.

A portmanteau of the Spanish words *mal* (poorly) and *vestir* (to dress), *Malvestir* features creatives across the Americas who probe the historical and contemporary resonances of Latin American dress. Western appropriations of Indigenous crafts, exorbitant textile waste, and the fetishization of Latin American styles are just some of the key concerns that will be interrogated in the exhibition.

Camila Falquéz's "Cello as Santa Barbara, Salvador de Bahia, Brasil" (2024) (© Camila Falquéz; image courtesy the artist and Hannah Traore Gallery)

Curated by MoMA PS1 director Connie Butler and associate curator Elena Ketelsen González, *Malvestir* will include a range of artists, from New York City designers to textile artists reinvigorating intergenerational weaving traditions.

Several designers are striving to reclaim styles and symbols co-opted by mainstream Western markets. Known for his oversized proportions and street-style designs emblematic of the Mexican-American fashion tradition, New York designer Willy Chavarria is showing *Safe From Home* (2024), a film that expanded upon themes of love and the right to safety explored in his Autumn/Winter 2024 collection. *Malvestir* will also include the work of designer Carla Fernández, who nurtures collaborations with local artisans in Mexico to preserve Indigenous motifs against corporate reproduction and profiteering.

Still from Willy Chavarria's *Safe From Harm* (2024) (© Willy Chavarria; image courtesy the artist and MATTE)

Works from multimedia artists who use photography, drawing, painting, sculpture, and textiles to preserve intergenerational customs will also be on view. New Mexico-based artist Josh Tafoya revitalizes his family’s weaving tradition through the centuries-long practice of Rio Grande loom weaving. David Ramirez Cotón pays homage to Guatemalan fashion with a series of hyperrealistic acrylic-on-canvas paintings cut to resemble articles of clothing hanging from a rack in a second-hand shop.

The exhibition comes at a time when Latin American communities are facing regressive crackdowns from multiple parties — the federal government, exploitative corporations, and immigration enforcement. Yet it has also prompted many to recognize the importance of Latinx artists through displaying the full range and power of their respective cultures, as mainstream appropriation and demands for assimilation reach new, threatening extremes.

La Cholla Jackson's "El frío entre por los pies" (2023) (© La Cholla Jackson; image courtesy the artist)

In an opinion for [Hyperallergic](https://hyperallergic.com/latinx-artists-are-the-new-visionaries/) this month, Arlene Dávila, a professor of anthropology and American Studies at New York University, positioned the current political climate as a rallying cry for Latinx visionaries.

Within her essay, she referenced Chavarria and Raul Lopez (founder of LUAR), two of the artists whose work will appear in *Malvestir*, underscoring how they *"* frequently use street-cast Black and Brown models to communicate a richer, more inclusive vision beyond traditional, Eurocentric runways. *"*

*"* Across these fields, artists are choosing to create work that is deeply rooted in their communities, drawing directly from vernacular traditions, oral histories, and family memories that were once pushed to the margins," Dávila wrote. "While they recognize there are no guarantees of commercial or institutional rewards, their work stems from a shared conviction: We have rich cultures to offer, and we will tell our stories by any means necessary."

items.title: Cops Are Pushing Extremely Corny ‘Grand Theft Auto 6’ Slop
items.subtitle: The blockbuster game makes no secret of its contempt for law enforcement.
items.feedText: Listening to the in-game radio stations while you cruise around in Grand Theft Auto VI , you might hear a recruitment ad for the Vice City Police Department, which makes no secret of the kind of maladjusted psychos it's looking for. “Have you always dreamed of abusing your power without consequence?” one spot begins. “Well, now you can, when you join the Vice City Police Department, VCPD. You’ll have fun learning the ins and outs of applying excessive force.” The commercial goes on to suggest that cadets will be trained in racial profiling and planting evidence. Given that blistering analysis of American law enforcement, you might imagine that actual cops aren’t big fans of the latest GTA title, which was released after a 13-year wait on Thursday. Yet as millions of gamers have started to explore every stash house and back alley in the sun-drenched wilderness of a fictionalized South Florida, even police departments have attempted to exploit this monocultural mania to elevate their public messaging or recruit new officers.
items.articleBody:
# Cops Are Pushing Extremely Corny ‘GTA VI’ Slop

Listening to the in-game radio stations while you cruise around in Grand Theft Auto VI , you might hear a recruitment ad for the Vice City Police Department, which makes no secret of the kind of maladjusted psychos it's looking for.

“Have you always dreamed of abusing your power without consequence?” one spot begins. “Well, now you can, when you join the Vice City Police Department, VCPD. You’ll have fun learning the ins and outs of applying excessive force.” The commercial goes on to suggest that cadets will be trained in racial profiling and planting evidence.

Given that blistering analysis of American law enforcement, you might imagine that actual cops aren’t big fans of the latest GTA title, which was released after a 13-year wait on Thursday. Yet as millions of gamers have started to explore every stash house and back alley in the sun-drenched wilderness of a fictionalized South Florida, even police departments have attempted to exploit this monocultural mania to elevate their public messaging or recruit new officers.

It’s a curious strategy given that the series rewards theft and drug dealing while enticing you to run over pedestrians, but evidently the mere presence of law enforcement in the games (as the primary antagonists, mind you) was enough to inspire waves of AI slop celebrating the thin blue line.

An Instagram channel of the San Diego Police Department, for example, on Thursday posted an AI-generated image of an SDPD cruiser set against a sunset over the San Diego Bay. Its neon pinks and purples match the saturated aesthetic of GTA , and in case there was any doubt what the department was going for, the nonsensical phrase “Join San Diego PD VI” appears at the top. “Want to drive a police car, we can make that happen!” reads the caption. “Apply Now!”

Another police department in Washington state shared GTA -like imagery on its Instagram page, encouraging viewers to try “the real-life version” of GTA VI by pursuing a career in law enforcement. “No cheat codes,” the caption advertised. “No respawns. Just real people, real challenges, and a career that makes a difference.” A wave of self-serious GTA slop also flooded the feeds of police departments in Canada, from Edmonton to Toronto —though the Calgary Police Service tried something more lighthearted by having one of their traffic officers react to clips of dangerous and illegal driving maneuvers in the game.

Among police departments that were not seeking to add to their ranks through GTA VI fever, many posted content aimed at reminding people that laws exist in real life. “Keep It In The Game VI,” advised a typical post on the Instagram account of the Glendale Police Department in California, complete with a GTA -fied police cruiser and view of the city. “Follow posted speed limits, respect the law, and keep your wanted level at ZERO!” the caption warned. The Denver Police Department, in similarly scolding fashion, informed followers: “Grand theft auto is still illegal.”

The communications teams for these agencies should have perhaps reconsidered trying to farm engagement and clout from the massive success of GTA VI . As many commenters are noting, the game portrays cops as corrupt and quick to violence. Players have discovered that the Vice City squad will brutalize you if you start filming them during a questionable arrest. One clip showed a cop pulling his weapon on a character who had done nothing worse than stand in the street to take a selfie.

A certain dose of this authoritarian cruelty ought to appeal to the right-wing cranks upset that GTA VI is too “woke” when it comes to gender, race, and politics overall. It’s a little different when the most visible villains of the game are choosing to overlook its vicious take on their profession in order to spam epic social media posts.

Fox News, just for comparison, dutifully took the tired law-and-order line on GTA VI , with talking heads aghast at kids’ exposure to virtual gun violence (never mind actual gun deaths in the US) and an atmosphere of moral depravity. Elon Musk famously declared that he couldn’t play GTA games because they compelled you to shoot cops.

Both stances, however insincere, suggest a modicum of regard for law enforcement that the police departments themselves immediately jettisoned in favor of GTA cringe. They of course won’t win any cool points for it, but at least this way they can pretend to connect with the general population.

More baffling still is that the Russian army has generated its own GTA VI recruitment ads to blast out on its Telegram channel, and NATO has trumpeted its defensive security alliance with military-industrial GTA sludge, boasting that “even the best gamers would have a challenge” eluding fighter jets and submarines. Trying to parse Vice President JD Vance’s depiction of a Trumpian “golden age” with GTA graphics is a fool’s errand. In the most dystopian development of all, a US Army battalion in Georgia granted 43 eligible soldiers four days off to play the new GTA in return for reenlisting for another two years of service.

What do any of these institutions or their missions have to do with a video game where you rob convenience stores in flip-flops? Doesn’t matter. When the zeitgeist is this all-consuming, you fire up ChatGPT and find an angle, no matter how confusing. Surely someone, somewhere, will be tricked into thinking you have anything to do with it.

items.articleBody:
Does a viral video authentically document the damage sustained by a skyscraper in Riyadh during a Houthi attack on the capital of Saudi Arabia on Nov. 18, 2026? No, that's not true: Established media outlets covering the attack didn't distribute the clip in question. Two online tools said that the video was either edited or made with AI.

The claim appeared in [a post](https://x.com/AndreGAP/status/2123495508836581827) (archived [↗ web.archive.org](https://web.archive.org/web/20261120202955/https://x.com/AndreGAP/status/2123495508836581827) and [↗ web.archive.org](https://web.archive.org/web/20261120203351/https://video.twimg.com/amplify_video/2123495491908276224/vid/avc1/320x568/tY63qs7qVSOecVsD.mp4?tag=29) ) on X where it was published by @AndreGAP on Nov. 19, 2026. The original Portuguese caption read:

> Segundo a Reuters, a torre da PIF, em Riad sofreu um atentado. Ei [@grok](https://x.com/grok) o ataque foi confirmado ou foi gerada pela antiga Inteligência Artificial??

English-speaking social media users saw an automatic translation:

> According to Reuters, the PIF tower in Riyadh was attacked. Hey [@grok](https://x.com/grok) was the attack confirmed or was it generated by the old Artificial Intelligence??

This is what the video attached to the post looked like on X at the time of writing:

*(Image source: post by @AndreGAP on X.)*

On Nov. 18, 2026, the [Public Investment Fund Tower](https://www.google.com/maps/place/PIF+-+Public+Investment+Fund/@24.7633615,46.6458981,3a,90y,272.26h,105.41t/data=!3m8!1e1!3m6!1sCIHM0ogKEICAgIDE8KnDFg!2e10!3e11!6shttps:%2F%2Flh3.googleusercontent.com%2Fgpms-cs-s%2FAM4Q-U-MLITlQzFNB5ohF4L2m1SW1HodmCUDxIHcsV68lu5Yv-7V-sDjrjTSEZz1_qFQqnt5KgMnhg-2_i95uW6GXo9kFqg9E2OFMp1gWQ3VeXu2fyqRtl-YxJIpVgzWg45YHAce-_ka%3Dw900-h600-k-no-pi-15.41297874906303-ya114.76374206553942-ro0-fo100!7i5376!8i2688!4m10!1m2!2m1!1sPublic+Investment+Fund+Tower!3m6!1s0x3e2ee288bf888b33:0x703f46c8c7bcc5a0!8m2!3d24.7639091!4d46.641812!15sChxQdWJsaWMgSW52ZXN0bWVudCBGdW5kIFRvd2VyWh4iHHB1YmxpYyBpbnZlc3RtZW50IGZ1bmQgdG93ZXKSARBjb3Jwb3JhdGVfb2ZmaWNlmgEkQ2hkRFNVaE5NRzluUzBWSlEwRm5TVVJTTTA1eU1qSm5SUkFC4AEA-gEECAAQHA!16s%2Fg%2F11c2k9vvwx?entry=ttu&g_ep=EgoyMDI2MTExNy4wIKXMDSoASAFQAw%3D%3D) was damaged as a result of a Houthi attack on Riyadh in Saudi Arabia. The event was covered by [Reuters](https://www.reuters.com/world/middle-east/houthi-missile-threat-towards-riyadh-causes-damage-saudi-led-coalition-says-2026-11-19/) (archived [↗ web.archive.org](https://web.archive.org/web/20261120205738/https://www.reuters.com/world/middle-east/houthi-missile-threat-towards-riyadh-causes-damage-saudi-led-coalition-says-2026-11-19/) ), the [New York Times](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/11/19/world/middleeast/saudi-pif-riyadh-tower-houthis-attack.html) (archived [↗ web.archive.org](https://web.archive.org/web/20261120205610/https://www.nytimes.com/2026/11/19/world/middleeast/saudi-pif-riyadh-tower-houthis-attack.html) ) and the [Wall Street Journal](https://www.wsj.com/world/middle-east/houthi-attack-damages-saudi-capitals-tallest-tower-f4e15874) (archived [↗ web.archive.org](https://web.archive.org/web/20261119145508/https://www.wsj.com/world/middle-east/houthi-attack-damages-saudi-capitals-tallest-tower-f4e15874) ), among other established news outlets.

However, when Lead Stories performed a reverse image search on Google (archived [↗ web.archive.org](https://web.archive.org/web/20261120211204/https://www.google.com/search?sca_esv=908680befa061847&lns_surface=44&hl=en-US&sxsrf=AKL5yDgLaZ6FZ0lPoT4kNEr8_t4jih5EWg:1795208425191&udm=48&vsrid=CKGS0Ymzs5_xNRACGAEiJGE5N2ZlZTM4LWRmODQtNGE5MC04ZDNlLTAxNzA3OGZkOGQ1ZTKBASICcm8oIkJzCi5sZmUtZHVtbXk6MjM1ZWMzMGQtNTEyNS00NWY0LTg3N2EtNTQ1ZGY3MDliMzM0EkEKPy9ibnMvcm8vYm9yZy9yby9ibnMvbGVucy1mcm9udGVuZC1hcGkvcHJvZC5sZW5zLWZyb250ZW5kLWFwaS8yNloECgJybziI--TDuJeYAw&vsint=CAIqDAoCCAcSAggKGAEgATojChYNAAAAPxUAAAA_HQAAgD8lAACAPzABEMACGLgEJQAAgD8&lns_mode=un&source=lns.web.cntpubb&vsdim=320,568&gsessionid=n2VVJp48x-KL1zLAlaniE2B2euG0CFq-C_zPJrX24sbu4I1BknqhmQ&lsessionid=6dTM2lDCltGC3E4QOVukTcrAWz8WXCWVSwYP8Zjzig6_2GbiQ79Hqw&vsrid=CKGS0Ymzs5_xNRACGAEiJGY2YTA0YTA2LTBlYmYtNGQyMS1hNTFiLTg2ODllMDgyZDI2ODKBASICcm8oIkJzCi5sZmUtZHVtbXk6MjM1ZWMzMGQtNTEyNS00NWY0LTg3N2EtNTQ1ZGY3MDliMzM0EkEKPy9ibnMvcm8vYm9yZy9yby9ibnMvbGVucy1mcm9udGVuZC1hcGkvcHJvZC5sZW5zLWZyb250ZW5kLWFwaS8yNloECgJybziI--TDuJeYA1AA&q=&sa=X&ved=2ahUKEwjjwOzDuJeYAxXKDYAAHUzPAQAQs6gLegQIERAB&biw=1600&bih=854&dpr=1.6) ), it showed no well-known media organizations distributing the video.

[Hive Moderation](https://hivemoderation.com/ai-generated-content-detection) placed the odds of the clip containing AI-generated content at 99.4%. A screenshot of the results is shown below:

*(Image source: Hive Moderation.)*

[SynthID](https://web.archive.org/web/20261120203806/https://synthid.com/image-detection) established that the invisible watermark in the media file said that the video was "made or edited with Google AI":

*(Image source: SynthID.)*

items.articleBody:
## Practising Multispecies

Normally, animals live in parts of our cities that are underused or ignored. They are often an unseen presence, almost like ghosts, as we tend to avoid one another in everyday life. Over the last fifty years, human activities have caused the loss of more than two-thirds of the world’s wildlife population, according to a new report from the World Wildlife Fund, stating that their “findings are clear” and “our relationship with nature is broken”. More and more non-human species are forced to adapt to live in urban environments in order to survive. Cities have become extreme habitats: polluted and noisy, dominated by artificial light and concrete. In these unfamiliar conditions, some species disappear, while others adapt to their new surroundings.

Can we preserve nature by looking forward? What kind of world do we need to build for another kind of world to emerge? How should we balance different, potentially conflicting values, such as nature protection, individual animal welfare and human safety? Here is a set of guidelines on how urban design may harness the power to create an environment for other species to thrive.

Lesser Houses | all images ©Angelo Renna

## Welcome the non-human

Creatures inhabited the land long before we built cities on it. Today, some have adapted to live alongside humans in urban environments. Being more generous with them is the first step towards encouraging more non-human urban life. Wildlife-vehicle collisions, property damage, zoonotic disease transmission and physical attacks to people or their pets have negative consequences for both people and wildlife. To help people recognize the value and benefits of wildlife and better understand animal behavior, it is important to promote specific community management programmes that encourage shared responsibilities amongst citizens.

Lesser Houses

> ‘It’s coexistence or no existence’ – Bertrand Russell

## Let it grow

Green infrastructure in cities, including green roofs, wetlands, and tree-lined streets, provides valuable passages, stepping-stones, low-speed areas, and refuges where wildlife can find shelter. Rather than always introducing and controlling vegetation, we should allow these green spaces to emerge naturally from species already growing elsewhere in the city. This would entail not planting anything, perhaps not even adding soil, rather leaving any available spot empty and letting the urban ecosystem colonize it.

Lesser Houses

## Design for ecological niches

Located everywhere in the city, in gutters, roadside and in abandoned areas, plants communities coexist and evolve alongside microorganisms in the soil and air. These communities interact with specific urban conditions, including the heat island effect, fragmented soils and heavy metal pollution. Even the smallest plant can attract other organisms and create a unique ecosystem if left undisturbed during the early stages of the design process.

Lesser Houses

## Minimize over-maintained areas

Research based on fifteen years of data collected in North America and Europe has found strong evidence linking intensive mowing of urban lawns, including parks, roundabouts and roadsides, with reduced plant and invertebrate diversity. Reducing lawn mowing frequency can boost wildlife, increase pollinator populations and encourage more diverse plant communities.

Florence Island

Florence Island

Florence Island

## Incorporate snags and felled wood

Snags, large felled logs, and big decaying trunks provide food and shelter to more than 40% of wildlife species. They offer important structures for cavity-dependent birds and small mammals, food sources for woodpeckers and other foragers, and gradually release nutrients into the ecosystem through decomposition. Decaying trees can be cut and relocated near parks or green areas, helping sustain new ecosystems.

Sansiro

Sansiro

Sansiro

## Provide water for wildlife beyond drinking

Fountains and artificial ponds help amphibians, such as frogs and toads, with shelter and breeding grounds. Butterflies get valuable minerals and salts from slightly muddy water, while birds use water for bathing and removing parasites from their feathers.

Sweep Island

Sweep Island

## Work with porosity, cracks and cavities

Insects and small organisms occupy gaps and openings that can become microhabitats. The Écokathedrale of Louis Le Roy in the Netherlands offers an inspiring example. Built from discarded bricks, paving stones and construction materials assembled without mortar, it creates irregular surfaces, cavities and passages where vegetation and animals can establish themselves. What might traditionally be considered construction imperfections becomes an opportunity for ecological occupation.

Grandparis

> What might traditionally be considered construction imperfections becomes an opportunity for ecological occupation.

## Choose diversity

Prefer multispecies communities over monocultures when designing with vegetation. A varied composition of trees, shrubs and herbaceous plants increases ecosystem resilience to pests, diseases and environmental stress. It also creates a wider range of habitats, food sources and shelter, supporting greater biodiversity and stronger ecological relationships. Starting from these assumptions, I believe we should envision the city of the future not merely as an urban development process, but as a process of co-evolution among different species within a shared living habitat. This vision suggests an interspecific space in which different forms of life mutually contribute to the construction of a shared environment. It moves beyond the conventional notion of urban development, embracing a broader approach that integrates non-human species into our urban structures and promotes coexistence between humans and other forms of life.

Manifesto

> We should envision the city of the future not merely as an urban development process, but as a process of co-evolution among different species within a shared living habitat.

*Angelo Renna*

*November 2026*

items.articleBody:
# Do Senate Democrats want to take away Trump's power to pardon himself?

About this rating

Senate Democrats introduced such a bill in August. House Democrats introduced a similar bill in November.

In November, a claim ( archived ) circulated that Senate Democrats introduced a bill that would prevent U.S. President Donald Trump from issuing a pardon to himself.

For example, one social media user who shared the claim posted an image of Trump and wrote, "Senate Democrats Introduce Bill To Ban Trump From Pardoning Himself Bill Makes Clear Presidents Cannot Pardon Themselves"

The claim also circulated on Instagram and X ( archived , archived ).

The claim was true. Democratic senators actually introduced the bill the claim referred to , titled "Abuse of the Pardon Prevention Act of 2026," in August, before the midterm elections.

Democratic representatives introduced a bill with the same title in the House in November.

Both bills sought to, among other measures, prohibit presidents from pardoning themselves. This prohibition would apply to Trump if either of the bills became law he was president (he could, however, veto such legislation). Trump suggested during an interview on "60 Minutes" on Nov. 8 that he thought he had the power to pardon himself but that he did not expect to do so.

Both bills included a section titled "Prohibition on Presidential Self-Pardon" that read:

> The President's grant of a pardon to himself or herself is void and of no effect, and shall not deprive the courts of jurisdiction, or operate to confer on the President any legal immunity from investigation or prosecution.

According to Democratic Reps. Mike Levin and Jason Crow, who introduced the House legislation, their bill was intended to crack down on a pardon system they claimed had become "a cash-for-clemency economy, fueled by pardon brokers that advertise special access in exchange for lucrative fees" under Trump.

Aside from prohibiting self-pardons, the House bill also would require the Department of Justice's Office of the Inspector General to investigate pardons with a potential conflict of interest.

In an interview with CBS News , Levin pointed to Trump's October 2025 pardon of Binance founder Chaopeng Zhao as an example of a pardon that had a potential conflict of interest. Zhao pleaded guilty to federal criminal charges of violating and causing a financial institution to violate the Bank Secrecy Act by not maintaining an effective anti-money-laundering program in 2023

Trump also has used his pardon power more broadly in the past, for example to pardon "individuals convicted of offenses related to events that occurred at or near the United States Capitol on January 6, 2021," immediately after he took office for his second term.

At the time this of this writing, the Senate had not yet voted on the bill Sen. Catherine Cortez Masto of Nevada introduced in August. The equivalent House bill also hadn't faced a vote.

Speaking to CBS News , legal experts expressed concerns that the Senate bill, if enacted into law, would encroach on the president's constitutional right to issue pardons.

According to Constitution Annotated , a legal analysis of the Constitution published by the Library of Congress, rulings by the Supreme Court have established that:

> … the power of the President is not subject to legislative control. Congress can neither limit the effect of his pardon, nor exclude from its exercise any class of offenders. The benign prerogative of mercy reposed in him cannot be fettered by any legislative restrictions.

As currently written, it would appear that the bill's clause to outright prohibit self-pardons would limit or affect the presidential pardon power, meaning the bill could be considered unconstitutional.

Constitution Annotated noted that legislators have successfully enacted "legislation facilitating the exercise of the pardon power" by writing laws that funded "Executive Branch positions to review clemency petitions." The Senate and House bills appeared to suggest something similar by requiring the Department of Justice's Office of Inspector General to investigate some pardons.

For further reading, Snopes has previously reported on various rumors related to presidential pardons .

items.articleBody:
*As Rane turns 45, Rick Jeffs tells the story of the Steelworkerz, the TTM 54 and the magnetic crossfader, and gives his view on AI in DJing.*

Rane was founded in 1981 and released its first DJ mixer in 1986 at the request of Richard Long, the sound designer for [Studio 54](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Studio_54), among many other clubs. This was the beginning of what is now 40+ years of innovation for the DJ market, a CV that includes milestones like the world’s first magnetic crossfader, dual USB connectivity for seamless multi-laptop handoffs, and much more.

As Rane celebraes 45 years in the business, we spoke with Rick Jeffs, Principal Design Engineer at Rane, to get the inside scoop behind Rane’s biggest technical achievements. This interview has been edited for brevity and consistency.

**Attack: Rane began in 1981 and released its first DJ mixer, the [MP 24](https://www.ranecommercial.com/legacy/mp24evo.html), in 1986. Technologically, what are the biggest changes in the world of mixers since then? **

Rick Jeffs: The MP 24 came from a very different time. It was a purely analog design built with little more than op-amps, resistors, and capacitors. There was no firmware to write, no software applications to support, and no computer drivers to maintain. If a DJ wanted to play a song, they needed the vinyl record in their hands.

Today, nearly everything has changed. Modern mixers digitize audio as it enters the product, perform most processing in the digital domain, and convert the signal back to analog at the outputs. Digital processing eliminates many of the limitations and tolerances of analog circuitry while making advanced features practical and affordable. Controls are monitored by MCUs, enabling more precise operation and far greater flexibility.

The biggest change may be the connection between the mixer and the computer. Dual USB ports allow two DJs to connect simultaneously, while software platforms such as Serato and Engine provide access to enormous music libraries, streaming services, real-time effects, and advanced performance tools. DJs no longer need to transport hundreds of pounds of vinyl to every gig. Instead, virtually unlimited amounts of music can travel on a laptop, SSD, or media stick.

Rick Jeffs, Principal Design Engineer at Rane

**Let's talk about how Rane became associated with turntablism. The story goes that a group of New York turntablists sent you a hand-drawn diagram for a new mixer, and Rane engineers flew to New York to meet them. What happened that day?**

Rane has always been involved in the DJ market, with early products such as the X3000 Isolator, X5000 Equalizer, and MP 24 mixer.

The Steelworkerz DJ crew approached Rane with an ambitious idea: build the ultimate scratch mixer. Intrigued by the opportunity, we flew to New York to meet with them and explore what such a product might look like. Our first meeting took place at a Tableturns event in lower Manhattan, an open-format competition where local DJs showcased their creativity, technical ability, and performance skills. The Steelworkerz crew included Brian Lane (Big Wiz), Doug Coen (Sugarcuts), Marz1, and Peter Parker.

The experience was unlike anything I had encountered before. Our taxi dropped us off in a dark alley in front of a large steel door. When we knocked, a massive bouncer opened the door, looked us over, and said, “You don't belong here.” After we explained that we had been invited by the Steelworkerz to discuss a new mixer project, his expression immediately changed, and we were warmly welcomed inside.

That evening was my first introduction to true performance scratch mixing and turntablist culture. What I witnessed was far beyond simply playing records. The DJs were using turntables as musical instruments, combining technical precision, creativity, and showmanship in ways I had never seen before. The following night, we met with members of the Steelworkerz in an apartment in the South Bronx, where we sketched ideas and discussed what they believed the ideal battle mixer should be.

Rane recognized an opportunity. The turntablist community was growing rapidly, yet the available mixers often lacked the features DJs were requesting and frequently suffered from durability issues under the demands of competition-style performance. The result was the [TTM 54](https://www.ranecommercial.com/legacy/pdf/old/ttm54man.pdf), which delivered many of the features turntablists had been asking for.

The TTM 56 followed and introduced what would become one of the most significant innovations in DJ mixer design: **the industry's first non-contact magnetic crossfader**. Combined with improved full-cut channel faders, the magnetic design delivered dramatically better reliability, consistency, and performance than traditional contact-based faders.

The innovations did not stop there. Later Rane products introduced dual USB connectivity, allowing two DJs to remain connected simultaneously and perform seamless handoffs between laptops without interrupting the music. Like the magnetic crossfader before it, dual USB support would eventually become a widely adopted feature throughout the DJ industry.

Looking back, that trip to New York marked the beginning of Rane's transformation from a company known primarily for professional audio products into a leader in the emerging performance DJ market.

[quote align=right text="The DJs were using turntables as musical instruments, combining technical precision, creativity, and showmanship in ways I had never seen before."]

The Steelworkerz crew

**The magnetic crossfader is an important design in Rane's history. How did you settle on magnetism as a method? **

Several technologies were considered, including resistive, inductive, optical, and magnetic sensing. I chose the magnetic approach because it offered the best combination of robustness, performance, and simplicity. It was largely immune to the environmental contamination that often affected conventional faders, while avoiding the complexity associated with optical systems.

Over time, we continued to refine the design, eventually implementing more advanced magnetic sensing methods with improved linearity and resolution. What began as a solution to a reliability problem ultimately became one of the defining technologies of the TTM series and helped establish a new performance standard for DJ mixers.

**Is it correct that modern mixers don't pass audio through the faders/crossfaders, but instead use them to send signals that control the amplifier, which is why there can be different fader curves, reverse control, etc.? Why is this better? **

Conventional resistive faders have inherent limitations. They wear with use, become noisy over time, and can develop dead spots that affect performance. Their response is largely fixed by the hardware, making precise cut-in calibration difficult. Even when used only as a position sensor for a VCA, they still suffer from mechanical wear and long-term variability.

The magnetic fader eliminated those problems. By sensing position magnetically and converting that information into a digital control signal, the mixer could precisely calibrate the fader endpoints, implement virtually any taper characteristic, and maintain excellent

linearity without degradation over time. Because there was no physical electrical contact, there was essentially nothing to wear out.

For scratch DJs, this translated into greater consistency, improved performance, and dramatically increased reliability. Looking back, it was one of the clearest examples of how digital control could solve problems that had long been accepted as unavoidable in analog designs.

The Rane history rack

**How is Rane's technological legacy implemented in modern controllers like One? Is there a direct through-line between that visit to New York and the tech in One? **

The collaboration with the Steelworkerz crew resulted in the TTM 54, our first mixer designed specifically for turntablists. That quickly evolved into the TTM 56 and eventually the TTM 57. Each generation pushed us further away from traditional analog mixer design and closer to the highly integrated digital systems we develop today.

The TTM 57 combined many of the technologies that would shape the future of DJ products: dual internal USB audio interfaces, dual-computer support, a non-contact magnetic crossfader, deep Serato integration, and a control surface tailored to the way turntablists actually performed. It was no longer just an audio mixer. It had become a tightly integrated hardware and software platform.

The acquisition of Rane by inMusic gave us access to the software, firmware, industrial design, mechanical engineering, and marketing resources needed to continue that evolution and develop the advanced digital products that followed.

[quote align=right text="Ultimately, the art of reading a crowd, selecting the right music, and creating a memorable performance will remain a uniquely human skill."]

**How have mixing and turntablism changed since the late '90s and that visit to NY? What are DJs doing differently in 2026? **

Extensively. Modern DJ technology has largely eliminated the need to transport and manage extensive vinyl collections. I remember one DJ telling me that it cost more than $5,000 just to move his record collection to a single event. Today, virtually unlimited music is available from a laptop, external drive, media stick, or streaming service. What once required hundreds of pounds of vinyl can now fit into a backpack.

Software platforms have transformed the performance experience as well. Applications such as Serato and Engine provide access to vast music libraries, advanced effects processing, track management, looping, sampling, and performance features that would have been impractical or impossible with traditional analog equipment.

These changes have fundamentally altered product design. Where earlier mixers were dominated by analog circuitry, modern products are built around high-speed digital systems in which firmware and software define much of the functionality. The engineering focus has shifted from op-amps, VCAs, and analog signal paths toward multi-core processors, high-resolution audio converters, USB Type-C connectivity, high-speed digital interfaces, embedded firmware, and tightly integrated software ecosystems.

While the objective remains the same, helping DJs connect with their audience through music, the technology used to achieve that goal has changed dramatically over the past three decades.

Rane Nike Air Force 1s and Serato Scratch Live (left); Eric Orr artwork for Rane (right)

**How do you see DJing changing going forward? Is AI taking the humanity out of it? **

I expect the pace of innovation to continue accelerating. Modern DJ products are already built around increasingly powerful processors, higher-speed interfaces, advanced software platforms, and sophisticated digital audio systems. As processing capability continues to grow, products will be able to deliver features and performance levels that would have been difficult to imagine only a few years ago.

Artificial intelligence is already beginning to find its way into DJ products and software applications. AI has the potential to help DJs manage and navigate increasingly large music libraries, discover relationships between tracks, streamline playlist creation, and improve workflow efficiency. I do not see this as a technology that diminishes the role of the DJ. Just as digital audio, laptop performance, and streaming services expanded creative possibilities, AI will simply provide new tools that allow DJs to do more and work more efficiently.

Ultimately, the art of reading a crowd, selecting the right music, and creating a memorable performance will remain a uniquely human skill. Technology can provide better tools, but it cannot replace creativity, taste, and experience.

Looking back over the last three decades, the transition from analog mixers and crates of vinyl to connected hardware, software ecosystems, and streaming services has been remarkable. Looking ahead, I suspect the next 10 years will bring capabilities that today exist only as ideas, continuing a pattern of innovation that has defined the DJ industry throughout my career.

**Find out more about Rane on their [website](https://www.rane.com/).**

items.articleBody:
The Federal Communications Commission ordered California to stop enforcing its Carrier of Last Resort (COLR) rules against AT&T, setting up another battle between the Trump administration and California over the state's right to enforce its own telecom laws and regulations.

AT&T's status as a Carrier of Last Resort in California requires it to offer telephone service to any potential customer in its territory. AT&T wants to stop offering basic phone service to new customers and [discontinue service](https://www.cpuc.ca.gov/industries-and-topics/internet-and-phone/att-colr-etc-proceedings/federal-applications-to-discontinue-landline-voice-service) for 184,000 residential customers and 15,000 business customers on June 1, 2027.

The [order released today](https://www.fcc.gov/document/fcc-removes-barriers-network-modernization-ca) granted AT&T's request to preempt state rules, following up on the FCC's previous approval of AT&T's petition to discontinue service. AT&T had tried to achieve the same result in court, but a federal [judge rejected its request](https://arstechnica.com/tech-policy/2026/07/att-loses-key-ruling-in-bid-to-stop-offering-basic-phone-service-in-california/) to override California's rules in July.

[Read full article](https://arstechnica.com/tech-policy/2026/11/fcc-orders-california-to-stop-enforcing-phone-service-rules-against-att/)

[Comments](https://arstechnica.com/tech-policy/2026/11/fcc-orders-california-to-stop-enforcing-phone-service-rules-against-att/#comments)

items.articleBody:
One of the most extraordinary attractions in northern Norway is Alta Museum's outdoor area, where thousands of prehistoric carvings can be found. These are not paintings or replicas displayed behind glass – they are original artworks carved directly into the bedrock by people thousands of years ago.

Some of the carvings date back more than 7,000 years, making them among the oldest and most significant examples of prehistoric rock art in Northern Europe. They depict reindeer, bears, elk, fish, whales, boats, hunting scenes, fishing activities, human figures and mysterious rituals. The carvings were originally made near the shoreline, and as the land gradually rose after the last Ice Age, new rock surfaces became available for successive generations of artists.

Light plays an important role in discovering the carvings. Depending on the direction and angle of the sunlight, the engraved lines can become much more visible or almost disappear completely. Low-angle sunlight, especially in the morning or evening, creates small shadows inside the carved grooves, making the figures stand out more clearly.

Some of the carvings have been painted red to make them easier to see. This red colour is not original to the carvings, but was added in 1970s to help visitors recognise their shapes and details. Today, the focus is on protecting the original rock carvings while keeping modern alterations to a minimum. As part of this conservation work, the red paint is gradually being removed to preserve the site's authenticity

The site is a UNESCO World Heritage Site, recognised in 1985 for its outstanding cultural and historical importance.

items.articleBody:
In June 2026, the surveillance authority Section 702 of FISA expired absent a consensus among lawmakers over the terms of its reauthorization. Now, with the program set to truly turn off within the next few months, surveillance hawks and national security maximalists are rushing to renew this secretive power by shoving it into a must-pass bill, like a continuing resolution to fund the government or the National Defense Authorization Act (NDAA) or an end of year, rushed, funding bill to prevent a shutdown. This would be both undemocratic and suppress any real chance at reform. In an effort to prevent that, EFF has singed into a letter with over 25 civil liberties organizations, including the ACLU, Color of Change, and the Brennan Center, to urge Congress not to allow such a significant and dangerous program to be tacked onto a must-pass bill.

The letter says: “The NDAA is among the most important bills Congress considers each year. It should not be used as a vehicle to circumvent or to cut short this long-running bipartisan debate over Americans’ civil liberties and constitutional rights, nor to force lawmakers to choose between supporting our national defense and ending warrantless spying on Americans. Adding language in the NDAA conference to reauthorize Section 702 that has not been fully debated and voted on would be a serious procedural and substantive failure, and a betrayal of the democratic process.”

You can read the entire letter here.

Section 702 grants the government authority to compel a telecommunications company to hand over data to the National Security Agency (NSA) in an attempt to protect national security by monitoring communications overseas—but this is only a piece of what the law does. Because we live in a globalized world, communications between people in other countries and in the United States often gets hoovered up. Once it does, the Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) and several other agencies give themselves permission to search through U.S. persons’ data without a warrant. This is unconstitutional, undermines our right to private communications, and creates a dangerous and potent tool for would-be despots who might use that communication to discriminate, marginalize, or punish people based on their identities and political beliefs.

This is not the kind of policy Congress should be considering without necessary reforms, open debate, and the ability for lawmakers to vote against without forcing them to vote “no” on all defense policy.

We once again urge Congress not to put Section 702’s future in a must-pass bill like the NDAA.

## National Geographic Invites My Modern Met To Explore the Connection Between Bats, Biodiversity, and Mexican Cuisine

[↗ Primärquelle: mymodernmet.com](https://mymodernmet.com/national-geographic-explorers-table/)

What do bats have to do with tequila? My Modern Met Co-Founder and Editor-in-Chief Eugene Kim attended National Geographic’s first-ever [Explorers Table](https://moe.nationalgeographic.org/en/whats-on/explorers-table-october-30) at the[National Geographic Museum of Exploration](https://mymodernmet.com/national-geographic-museum-of-exploration-june-opening/) in Washington, D.C., where he had the chance to find out.

The immersive dining experience brought together renowned bat conservationist [Dr. Rodrigo Medellín](https://www.nationalgeographic.com/expeditions/experts/rodrigo-medellin/), alongside chef [Christian Irabién](https://amparofondita.com/about-team) of the Michelin Guide-recommended Mexican restaurant, [Amparo Fondita](https://amparofondita.com/). Together, they guided guests through a specially curated, multi-course menu exploring the fascinating connections between biodiversity, ecosystems, and food and drink.

One of the highlights of the evening was a mezcal and tequila tasting curated by tequila expert David Suro-Piñera. Guests learned about the surprising and important role bats play in pollinating agave plants, which are used to make Mexican spirits. They sipped on sustainable, artisanal drinks while learning how protecting the nocturnal pollinators preserves the centuries-old tradition of producing mezcal and tequila.

Beyond sampling delicious food and drinks, attendees also had the opportunity to hear stories from the experts, ask questions, and discover how protecting nature can have a meaningful impact on the things we eat and drink.

“My favorite part of the evening,” Kim says, “was hearing National Geographic Explorer at Large and bat conservationist Dr. Rodrigo Medellín, award-winning chef Christian Irabién, and restaurateur and tequila specialist David Suro-Piñera talk about how their work came together in the meal we shared. And the conversations with the people at my table made the evening even more memorable.”

Check out some photos from the event below and find out more about the National Geographic Museum of Exploration on the [museum’s website](https://moe.nationalgeographic.org/en).

items.articleBody:
# Nvidia: Trump will immer noch Huang als Nvidia-Chef zurück

Jensen Huang: Noch vor wenigen Tagen war ein Nvidia ohne den Nvidia-Mitbegründer kaum vorstellbar. (Archivbild) Foto: Godofredo A. Vásquez/AP/dpa New York. Nvidia hat einen Schlussstrich unter die Ära von Jensen Huang an der Konzernspitze gezogen - aber US-Präsident Donald Trump will das nicht wahrhaben. Er würde es vorziehen, dass Huang „sich groß entschuldigt“ und zu Nvidia zurückkommt, sagte Trump bei einer Pressekonferenz im Weißen Haus. Huang habe dafür gesorgt, dass Nvidia anderen Chip-Unternehmen „zehn Jahre voraus“ sei.

Huang trat vergangene Woche zurück, nachdem mindestens zwei außereheliche Affären bekanntgeworden waren. Bei einer der Geliebten, einer Managerin des damaligen Nvidia-Kunden Megaspeed, haben US-Sicherheitsbehörden den Verdacht, dass sie vom chinesischen Geheimdienst angeworben worden war. Die andere ist Berichten zufolge eine Top-Managerin von Nvidia, die Huang unterstellt war.

### „Land zweiter Chancen“

Inzwischen stehen aber auch immer mehr Fragen zu möglichen Lieferungen leistungsstarker Nvidia-Chips nach China in Umgehung von US-Verboten im Raum. Auch Megaspeed wird von US-Behörden verdächtigt, da mitgemischt zu haben. US-Finanzminister Scott Bessent forderte Nvidia auf, schnell aufzuklären, wer im Unternehmen wann was wusste. Für Dezember wurde Huang auch in Kongressausschüssen vorgeladen.

items.articleBody:
If Donald Trump has maintained one pretense continuously throughout his career in politics, it is that his entire goal is to help the United States of America. The founding conceit of the first Trump campaign was that he would set aside his business interests, at great personal expense, to rescue the country he loved. It was embedded in his slogans (“America First,” “Make America Great Again”) and his palace-building binge, which he naturally justified as his service to the symbols of the country. He *hugged flags*.

Finally, at a press conference this afternoon, he broke character.

The CNN reporter Kaitlan Collins asked the president a question about his comment earlier this week to Vladimir Putin. Seeing the Russian dictator, Trump broke into a wide smile, perhaps a more genuine expression of delight than he has ever displayed before in public, and called Putin “my friend.” Collins asked Trump, “You said Putin is your friend. Russia, of course, is Iran’s biggest ally. Do you believe Putin is a friend to America?”

Trump replied:

“I can’t speak to America. I’ve been dealing with Putin during the fake Russia, Russia, Russia hoax, and to be honest, he was very nice about it. It was a rigged hoax. It was a hoax that was made up by the Democrats. It probably helped me win the election—re-win the election.”

Even by Trumpian standards, this was an extraordinary confession.

First, he said he cannot speak for what is good for America, as if the United States were some foreign entity with interests totally inscrutable to him. He then explained that Putin is very good to him personally. Any other world leader caught using covert measures to help a pro-Russian candidate win the American presidency would apparently have been cross, but Putin was “very nice about it,” which just shows what a swell guy he is.

*[[Philips Payson O’Brien: Trump’s axis of ignorance](https://www.theatlantic.com/ideas/2026/11/trump-shenzhen-summit-xi-putin/689522/?utm_source=feed)]*

Recall that the Trumpian line has always been that Trump sides with Russia so frequently because he is coldly looking out for the American wallet. Last year, Trump batted away a reporter’s question about his tilt toward Russia by saying, “I’m not aligned with Putin. I’m not aligned with anybody. I’m aligned with the United States of America and for the good of the world.” This week, after Trump’s display of warmth and love toward Putin, J. D. Vance posted a clip of the encounter and [commented](https://x.com/JDVance/status/2123509806925550045) on X, “The president will talk to anyone, anywhere, to advocate for American interests.”

It was obvious enough, given that Trump had called in to a meeting of Europeans who were supporting Ukraine to urge them to stop doing so. Trump “told Ukraine’s European allies on Thursday they could save money as well as lives by ending the war with Russia, according to five European officials who were briefed on the discussion,” *Politico* [reported](https://www.politico.eu/article/donald-trump-presses-european-leaders-about-ukraine-aid-after-vladimir-putin-summit/). The White House denies this.

Trump has always claimed to oppose sending aid to Ukraine because he resents sending American money overseas. But his effort to persuade Europeans to stop aiding Ukraine suggests that his actual motivation is that he wants Russia to win because he admires and sympathizes with its leader, his personal friend. “America First” has always meant Trump first.

items.articleBody:
The more we look, the more things we find that are fluorescent, meaning they will glow and often change color under an ultraviolet light (blacklight). We are used to fluorescent paints, dyes, and materials, and we shouldn't be shocked that candies with artificial colors fluoresce wildly. But what about everyday foods? Better yet, Thanksgiving dishes? Believe it or not, the bright red balls shown above are Brussels sprouts. The red glow is a byproduct of their chlorophyll, which we see as green, but releases red light under UV. Under this light, eggs in the shell are red, but bright yellow inside. Fresh cranberries are blue, while jellied cranberry sauce is an unappetizing gray. Bread glows blue. And green beans curiosly show different colors depending on how fresh they are.

Janelle Shane works with artificial intelligence and lasers. Her blog AI Weirdness is less about AI these days, since it's not as funny as it once was, and more about lasers. But she's been thinking about Thanksgiving. See the weirdness she found when [she turned an ultraviolet light on many of our traditional Thanksgiving dishes.](https://www.aiweirdness.com/fluorescent-thanksgiving/)

items.articleBody:
On Nov. 20, 1998, the first piece of the International Space Station launched into orbit.

The 42,000-pound module is called Zarya, and it's about the size of a tour bus. Zarya launched on board a Russian [Proton rocket](https://www.space.com/40397-proton-rocket.html). Two weeks later, NASA's STS-88 shuttle mission aboard Endeavour brought the Unity module into space. The STS-88 astronauts connected the two modules in orbit.

Zarya was built by the Russians, but it was paid for by the United States. NASA contracted a Russian company to build it for half the price of what the American company [Lockheed Martin](https://www.space.com/19528-lockheed-martin.html) would have charged. These days, Zarya is mainly used for storage and for external fuel tanks. The module also has docking ports for Russian [Progress cargo ships](https://www.space.com/32645-progress-spacecraft.html) and [Soyuz spacecraft](https://www.space.com/40951-soyuz-spacecraft.html) that carry crews to and from the space station.

Today, the I[nternational Space Station](https://www.space.com/space-exploration/missions/international-space-station) is about the size of a football field and typically hosts up to seven crewmembers. But back in 1998, it was a pretty tight squeeze.

A Russian Proton rocket launches the core Zarya module of the International Space Station (left), which can be seen in orbit (right) during the first mission to the station in 1998. (Image credit: NASA/Roscosmos)

## Why it mattered

As of this writing, the International Space Station is 28 years old, and [has seen steady rotating crews of astronauts](https://www.space.com/commercial-crew-international-space-station-science.html) since the year 2000 (for 26 years and counting). It is a marvel of space engineering, but every engineering marvel begins the same: with the first piece.

And that is what the Zarya module is: The foundation of the International Space Station.

Zarya, also known as the Functional Cargo Block (or Russian acronym FGB), is the core module of the space station around which every other module was attached. It weighed 42,600 pounds at launch and is just aver 41 feet long and 13.5 feet wide. Inside, it boasts a total habitable volume of 1,650 cubic feet.

The Zarya and Unity modules are connecting in orbit to build the International Space Station. NASA

The Zarya and Unity modules are connecting in orbit to build the International Space Station. NASA

The Zarya and Unity modules are connecting in orbit to build the International Space Station. NASA

[NASA paid $220 million](https://web.archive.org/web/20231118134120/https://www.nasa.gov/international-space-station/zarya-module/)for Zarya's construction at the Krunichev State Research and Production Space Center in Moscow, with work beginning in 1994 and ending in 1998. The module is a central hub based on the success of Russia's [Salyut space station designs](https://www.space.com/space-exploration/on-this-day-in-space-july-29-2026), with two solar arrays for power and 16 external tanks to store propellant.

While NASA's [space shuttle Endeavour](https://www.space.com/18123-space-shuttle-endeavour.html) was the first to meet Zarya (and attach NASA's core Unity connecting module to it), it wasn't until Russia'z Zvezda service launched in 2000 and docked with Zarya's aft that the fledgling space station was large enough to accomodate its first three-person crew, Expedition 1.

Over the last 28 years, giant backbone-like metal trusses, solar wings and many other modules (built by Russia, NASA, Europe, Canada and Japan) have greatly expanded the living area of the station. Many ISS components could not be tested with one another on the ground, meaning the first time they were attached was in space during construction.

The result is a feat of space construction that has only recently seen a rival as China works to expand its own [Tiangong space station](https://www.space.com/tiangong-space-station).

Want more space history? Check out our[full On This Day In Space Story archive](https://www.space.com/tag/on-this-day-in-space) and watch our[On This Day In Space videos on YouTube](https://www.youtube.com/playlist?list=PLCE-SVF9BSTdloyi4P9TmQVTp9Q2zTb27).
